title: Prove actual OGD versus mean-predictor loss gap for the guessing game
head: codex/research-online-guessing-migration
body:
Example2.14 states that the horizon-tuned OGD rate is suboptimal for the guessing game. This package adds a direct formal comparison on the same all-zero label stream: the actual strict-prefix mean predictor has cumulative square loss1/4, while the actual projected OGD loss is at least n/4 at T=(2n)^2. The resulting gap is at least n/4-1/4 and exceeds any real threshold at some n above any natural cutoff.

Three new public proofs close this comparison through the actual two algorithms and an Archimedean witness. OGD starts at1, the source mean predictor at1/2; each OGD run uses its known positive horizon. The terminal is unbounded-tail existence, not an equal-initialization, every-stream, every-initialization, single-anytime-run, Tendsto, minimax or Chapter4 guarantee. These are derived refinements, not three numerical theorems printed in the book. The source real[0,1] labels, prediction-before-feedback order, true projection/gradient and produced global square regularity are retained. The printed O(sqrtT) and derived constant2sqrtT are distinguished.

Nine existing public proofs and one domain definition are revalidated with their mathematical tokens fixed; the two original canary modules are bytefixed. A new nondegenerate canary compares both actual algorithms at n4/T64/eta1/16 and proves a gap at least3/4. Eight source-review reader corrections and the five-step proof bridge are integrated into the existing shared Book route.
